title: Steward: unified admin utility synthesis and runbook-as-task compiler
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build 'Steward', a synthesis layer that compiles existing runbooks and admin snippets into typed, idempotent tasks that can be executed from the Console, called from the admin API, or used in dry-run/simulation environments. Steward should: 1) accept declarative runbook fragments (YAML/MD) and produce a typed task manifest with input schema, output contracts, provenance and required RBAC; 2) auto-instrument telemetry (trace/correlation id, tokenized cost estimate, step durations, error codes) and emit standardized events for Console dashboards; 3) wrap destructive actions in safety gates (preview, dry-run, canary execution mode, escalation hooks); 4) provide a sandboxed executor for simulated runs with deterministic mocks; 5) expose a runtime adapter to integrate with existing admin microservices and the ops CLI.
acceptance_criteria: Runbook fragments authored in the new DSL compile to a Task Manifest with JSON Schema for inputs and outputs
Console renders a generated task with input form from schema and shows pre-execution cost and latency estimate
Task executions emit telemetry events (task.start, step.complete, task.error) with correlation_id and token estimates
Safety modes: preview (no-op), dry-run (mocked external effects), and canary (limited scope) are supported and selectable
Idempotency guarantees for retry: tasks must include a replay-safe execution key and be checkpointable
Documentation + PR with end-to-end demo (Drive doc + GitHub PR) merged to main branch
comments: 2025-02-10 - Aisha: Initial scoping completed during triage. Decided to try a compact DSL (YAML-first) that maps to typed manifests and to reuse the existing runlet step library where possible.

2025-02-13 - Marcel: Spike findings: converting 12 canonical runbooks to the DSL took ~2 engineer-days; main challenge is idempotency semantics for third-party APIs. Proposed adding a 'replay_key' and sequence checkpoints in the manifest.
2025-02-15 - Review (PM): Evan requested a clear migration path from legacy shell snippets to DSL and added requirement for token cost estimates on the preflight UI.
2025-02-17 - Design feedback: Priya asked for explicit safety labels (destructive|read-only|sensitive) in metadata and a visual guardrail in the Console. Added label mapping to manifest generator.

2025-02-19 - Engineering update: implemented prototype telemetry hooks and demoed task.start/task.end events. Observed step-level durations and a 12% overhead for instrumentation in local runs. Draft PR opened: see artifacts.
2025-02-20 - Blocker logged: need SRE signoff on sandbox network policies before enabling dry-run against production-adjacent services. Added ENG-1009008 as follow-up for policy automation.
implementation_notes: Implementation will be split into three deliverables: (A) DSL + compiler that emits Task Manifests (JSON Schema + metadata); (B) runtime adapters (Console form renderer, CLI hook, executor shim) and sandbox runner; (C) telemetry + safety gates. Prefer incremental approach: ship read-only tasks first (catalog migration), then introduce safety-wrapped mutating tasks. Use existing runlet library to minimize duplicated step implementations; implement a lightweight manifest linter as a gate in CI.
blockers: KMS permissions for simulated secrets in dry-run
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): expose Steward tasks in internal Console for SRE and firstline; Phase 2: allow ops CLI invocation and automated playbooks; Phase 3: enable self-serve for on-call with RBAC gating and audit logging. Each phase gated by acceptance tests and telemetry thresholds. Plan retention: run metadata & telemetry retained for 90 days in ops telemetry cluster.
next_steps: 1) Finish manifest schema and linter. 2) Complete sandbox network policy with SRE (ENG-1009008). 3) Merge telemetry PR and add Grafana dashboard panel. 4) Begin small canary migration of 3 non-destructive runbooks.
